+		// Enforce mode flags and the .goshs ACL on WebDAV verbs.
// Check Basic Auth and use middleware
+// webdavGuard wraps the webdav handler with mode-flag enforcement (read-only /
+// upload-only / no-delete) and the .goshs ACL. It is the choke point for the
+// "webdav" mux and is exercised directly in tests.
+// The verb gating reflects what golang.org/x/net/webdav actually does on disk:
+//   - MOVE always Rename()s the source (removing it from its original path) and,
+//     with Overwrite:T, RemoveAll()s an existing destination first. Both are
+//     deletions, so MOVE is blocked whenever deletion is disabled.
+//   - COPY to a fresh path only creates, but COPY with Overwrite (the library
+//     default unless the header is "F") onto an existing destination RemoveAll()s
+//     it first — also a deletion. That single case is gated behind the delete
+//     flags; a non-overwriting COPY stays allowed.
+		// Enforce the .goshs ACL on the addressed resource (proper 401 with a
+		// challenge), then hand the request to the ACL-aware FileSystem via the
+		// context so recursive PROPFIND walks stay filtered too.
+// webdavDestExists reports whether the Destination header of a COPY/MOVE
+// request already points at an existing resource inside the webroot. It is used
+// to distinguish an overwriting COPY (which deletes the destination) from a
+// harmless copy to a new path.
// webdavEnforceACL applies the .goshs ACL to the directly-addressed WebDAV
// resource, mirroring the HTTP server (sendFile/doDir). It is the choke point
// in wdGuard and, unlike the FileSystem layer below, can return a proper 401
// webdavACLTree builds a webroot with a public file and a password-protected
+// webdavModeTree builds a webroot with a file to protect (secret.txt) and an
+// existing file a MOVE/COPY could clobber (victim.txt).
+// davReq issues a WebDAV request (optionally with Destination/Overwrite headers)
+func davReq(t *testing.T, h http.Handler, method, target, dest, overwrite string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder {
+// MOVE renames (deletes) the source, so --no-delete must block it. Regression
+// for the residual GHSA gap where MOVE bypassed --no-delete.
+	require.Equal(t, "TOP-SECRET", fileContent(t, dir, "secret.txt"), "source must survive a blocked MOVE")
+	require.True(t, fileMissing(t, dir, "gone.txt"), "destination must not be created")
+// MOVE with Overwrite:T also RemoveAll()s the destination — --no-delete must
+// block it before the victim is destroyed.
+	require.Equal(t, "VICTIM", fileContent(t, dir, "victim.txt"), "existing file must not be clobbered")
+// COPY with Overwrite onto an existing destination RemoveAll()s it first, so
+	require.Equal(t, "VICTIM", fileContent(t, dir, "victim.txt"), "existing file must not be clobbered")
+// A COPY to a fresh path deletes nothing and must stay allowed under
+// --no-delete, even though the Overwrite header defaults to on.
+	require.Less(t, w.Code, http.StatusBadRequest, "non-overwriting COPY must be allowed")
+	require.Equal(t, "TOP-SECRET", fileContent(t, dir, "secret.txt"), "source must be untouched")
+// --upload-only forbids deletion too, so MOVE must be blocked there as well.
+// --read-only blocks every mutating verb, including MOVE and COPY.
+// Control: with no mode flags a MOVE works as usual — the source is renamed away
+// and the destination created. Confirms the guard does not over-block.
+	require.True(t, fileMissing(t, dir, "secret.txt"), "MOVE should remove the source")
